title: The submission of a guarantee claim on the target: no reference field, no channel interface, no state map, no timer home and no service event
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-014); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v3.md; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v2.md; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md; _work/msr/context/S3.md
description: Five values the submit slice needs are fixed by no source: the submission reference the legacy story records on the case, since guarantee_claim has eight fields and none holds a reference and the case field list is not read for this key; the interface of the TCG claim channel, since INT-29 says not available today and entered and filed by the guarantee officer and no operation, file or schema is published anywhere; the correspondence between the seventeen rule states of the guarantee state machine and the five members of LOV-CLAIM-STATUS, since only the claim row list and the case statuses exist; the home of the 2 and 5 working day timers of R-GUA-12 and R-GUA-21, since the legacy data table names the timer table and the ownership rows give S3 no job; and the event set of the service, since the ownership rows give S3 no event while the connection matrix shows rwb-reporting listening to it, so a submission raises no Kafka event.
evidence: TSDs and FSDs read for this key: TSD S3 T3.1 lists DF-TRT-015 to DF-TRT-022 as id, case_id, claim_type, claim_deadline, claimed_amount, filed_at, paid_amount and status, T3.2 lists LOV-CLAIM-STATUS as PREPARING, FILED, DEFECT, PAID and REJECTED, T4 states 32 rules over 17 states with no map to the list, T5.1 gives INT-29 as Both, not available today, entered and filed by the guarantee officer, and T5.3 gives Events None. The legacy story RWB-E4-014 says in AC1 that the submission reference is recorded on the case and its data table lists recovery_case, timer, v_ace_account, guarantee_claim, document and decision_log_entry. Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 gives R-GUA-12 a 2 working day timer with owner TCG and systems Workbench and TCG claim channel, and R-GUA-21 a 5 working day timer. The context pack ownership rows give S3 one table, two operations, zero events, zero jobs and one workflow, while Architecture v5 slide 13 has P9 Reporting listening to events of S3 and S3 reaching P3 by Temporal.
proposed: Carry the legacy sentences unchanged with their origin tags and record the target reading: the filing is written on guarantee_claim as status FILED with filed_at as the business date and no reference element is published until the Logical Data Model names a field identifier; the TCG claim channel is a recorded officer filing with no outbound call, file or queue until INT-29 publishes an interface; the claim status map fixes only PREPARING to FILED and the case statuses CLAIM_APPROVAL, CLAIM_PART_PAID and CLAIM_SUBMITTED stay rwb-case's; the two working-day timers are workflow and case timers written by rwb-case, with no timer table in rwb_guarantee; and the submission raises no Kafka event, its signal being the stage report to the parent CaseWorkflow.

title: The guarantee-claim resource contract: nothing to publish for the submission reference, for the TCG channel or for the text of the 409, and no retention rule for a claim row
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v2.md; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v3.md; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-014); _work/msr/context/S3.md
description: Four values of the contract slice are fixed by no source: the element that would carry the submission reference, since the eight fields of guarantee_claim hold none and the legacy story still records a reference on the case; the operation, callback or schema of the TCG claim channel, since INT-29 is not available today and is entered and filed by the officer; the business text of the 409 of an update on a claim that is already filed, since only the status list and the message catalogue exist and no message id covers it; and the retention and archive rule of a guarantee_claim row, which no source read for this key states.
evidence: TSD S3 T-A.1 gives two operations only - API-S3-001 POST /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/guarantee-claims with right C and the Idempotency-Key header, and API-S3-002 PATCH /api/recovery/v1/guarantee-claims/{claimId} with right U and idempotency not applicable - with the error statuses 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503, and T-A.2 names GuaranteeClaimRequest, GuaranteeClaimUpdate and GuaranteeClaim. TSD S3 T3.1 gives the eight fields of the row and T3.0 the seven standard columns; T5.1 gives INT-29 as not available today; T5.3 gives no event. The FSD S3 A2.2 rules are VR-S3-002-1, R-GUA-12, R-GUA-21 and BR-S3-002 and name no channel interface and no reference field. The legacy story names no message id for a 409 and no retention rule, and the message table of the legacy story holds MSG-GEN-001, MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P7-003 only.
proposed: Publish the resource as TSD S3 T-A.1, T-A.2 and T3.1 state it and nothing more: the two operations on base /api/recovery/guarantee/v1, the three schemas over DF-TRT-015 to DF-TRT-022, the guarantee_claim DDL template with the T3.0 columns, the six error statuses with the problem envelope, the Idempotency-Key rule, the versioning rule and the fakes; the 409 is published with its cause - a claim already in FILED - and its messageId slot, and its text waits for the C1 message catalogue; no reference element, no channel operation and no retention rule is declared, and the retention value is carried as the placeholder of this row.
